title: Applications of Quartz Sand in Petroleum Production and Engineering Material Selection:  A Comprehensive Review
content: Quartz sand is used throughout oil and gas well engineering, including hydraulic fracturing, wellbore sand control, high-temperature cementing and produced-water treatment, but each use imposes distinct require-ments on particle size, morphology, strength, reactivity and cleanliness. Following the performance chain from mineral source, washing and size classification, storage and transport, slurry injection and fracture placement to long-term service, this review discusses proppant transport and settling, bridging and bed-load migration, breakage and wall embedment under closure stress, fines migration, fracture-fluid residues, mul-tiphase and non-Darcy flow, stress cycling and time-dependent damage. Natural quartz sand, pre-cured and curable resin-coated sands, ceramic proppants and mixed proppants are compared. Material selection should be based on target-well long-term conductivity tests and life-cycle economics. The review also considers gravel packing, where grain-size matching to formation sand, screen compatibility and packing completeness are critical, and high-temperature well cementing, where finely ground silica regulates the calcium-to-silicon ra-tio of hydration products and mitigates strength retrogression. API Std 19C and ISO 13503-2:2024 provide the basic characterization framework, whereas ISO 13503-5:2006 can organize long-term conductivity compari-son but does not provide an absolute in-situ conductivity. A project-level test matrix, minimum reporting set and batch-traceability loop are proposed for resource assessment, product development, procurement and field verification.
